analysis:
Examined the reconnect-policy change.

CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift:
- runLoop (head L12-53) replaces the fixed ExponentialBackoff(1s..30s) with an injected CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.
- Each attempt now gets a CoordinatorSessionRecorder (L19). The delay is TimeInterval.random(in: policy.nextDelayRange(after: end)) (L31).
- session.markOpened() runs after sendRegistration (L186).
- The receive callback records a close-frame code on connectionQueue (L418-421) before error handling. The receive loop still throws on close frames and on empty non-control frames (L438-455).
- sentCloseCode (L513-522) reads two big-endian bytes only when the reported code is nil/noStatus and content.count>=2, so there is no out-of-bounds read. The close code is only logged (L33-35) and fed to the policy.

Unchanged, so no new data exposure:
- Registration, App Attest resume nonce generation and reset (L101-103, L115-116), TLS scheme selection and teardown.
- Telemetry fields, including coordinator_url, which was already present.

CoordinatorClient.swift adds a stored reconnectPolicy and an optional init parameter (head L120-141). CoordinatorClientState.swift adds a lock-guarded recorder (head L509-537).

Trust model: the close code comes from the trusted coordinator over the WebSocket (TB-002). It influences only local reconnect timing, not authorization or attestation. T-053 connection-binding is unaffected because the resume nonce is still per-connection.

Open question: CoordinatorReconnectPolicy, CoordinatorSessionEnd and the nextDelayRange implementation are not in the supplied units. Integration should verify three things, since T-010/A-018-style availability and coordinator reconnect storms depend on them:
1. The range is never empty or invalid, since TimeInterval.random(in:) traps on an empty Range; a trap would crash the provider.
2. Delays stay bounded and non-zero with jitter for short-lived sessions and attacker-unrelated close codes such as 1012/1008, so a rejected registration does not cause a tight reconnect loop against the coordinator.
3. The default CoordinatorReconnectPolicy() preserves at least the prior 30s cap/backoff semantics.

No concrete regression was identified in the visible code.
